eateries.name: Hareli Eco Resort Restaurant
eateries.signature_dish: Local Chhattisgarhi thali (chausela roti, aamat, dal)
eateries.why_it_matters: Inside the Chhattisgarh Tourism eco-resort at the sanctuary's Mohda gate - effectively the only sit-down dining within 20 km of Barnawapara, and the place that runs the post-safari breakfast for safari guests staying outside.
eateries.insider_tip: Order Chhattisgarhi thali rather than the standard Indian/Chinese menu; the kitchen does the regional dishes properly. Pre-book lunch if you've come on a day-safari, otherwise the kitchen runs out by 13:00.
eateries.signature_address: Hareli Eco Resort, Mohda, Barnawapara, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh 493551

eateries.name: CG Tourism Cottages Mess, Barnawapara
eateries.signature_dish: Veg thali with rice and dal
eateries.why_it_matters: The Chhattisgarh Tourism cottage cluster keeps a small in-house mess for guests - the second of the only two reliable cooked-meal options at the sanctuary, used by foresters and visiting researchers as much as by tourists.
eateries.insider_tip: Open only for cottage guests and pre-booked diners. Mains ₹90-170. Order at check-in for the same evening; same-day walk-in usually means you eat what's left.
eateries.signature_address: CG Tourism Cottages, Barnawapara Sanctuary Gate, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh 493551

eateries.name: Mahasamund Highway Dhabas
eateries.why_it_matters: Driving in or out of Barnawapara on the Mahasamund highway, the dhaba cluster is the realistic dinner stop - cleaner than the sanctuary tea stalls, faster than going into Mahasamund town.
eateries.insider_tip: Stop at one of the older Mor Mahanadi-style dhabas around the 30km mark from the sanctuary; truck volume is the proxy for kitchen freshness. Avoid late-night non-veg unless you've watched it being cooked.
eateries.signature_address: NH-353 Mahasamund-Saraipali stretch, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh

eateries.name: Sanctuary Forest Rest House Mess
eateries.why_it_matters: The Forest Department's rest-house mess inside the sanctuary serves only registered overnight guests, but offers the cleanest read of how the duty staff actually eat - rice, locally-sourced vegetables, mahua/imli pickle when in season.
eateries.insider_tip: Bookings via cgforest.com only; food-included tariff is the better choice. No alcohol. Power runs on solar plus generator; eat by 8:30pm.
eateries.signature_address: Forest Rest House, Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary, Mahasamund District 493551

eateries.name: Sanctuary Gate Tea Stalls
eateries.why_it_matters: Two thatched chai stalls outside the gate run a 5:30am opening to catch safari jeeps - the only food economy at the sanctuary edge before the Hareli kitchen lights up.
eateries.insider_tip: Cash only, no UPI. Stalls shut once the morning safari window closes around 8am and reopen at 14:00 for the evening departures.
eateries.signature_address: Outside Barnawapara Sanctuary main gate, Mahasamund District 493551

picks.name: Barnawapara Wildlife Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: The only established resort with direct access to Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary, offering guided tiger and gaur safaris from your doorstep.

picks.name: Barahi Guest House
picks.why_nakshiq: Clean, family-run rooms in central Barnawapara town with reliable WiFi and a restaurant serving local Chhattisgarhi thalis at half resort prices.

picks.name: Barnawapara Rest House (Forest Department)
picks.why_nakshiq: Situated 2 km from the sanctuary's main gate with forest department staff on-site to arrange same-morning safari bookings and walking trails.

jagdalpur.tagline: Chitrakote Falls and the Bastar tribal heartland

eateries.name: Bastar Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: The young-Bastar cafe near Dalpat Sagar lake - tribal-art murals on the walls, Farra and Tikhur on the menu next to pizza and pasta - and the closest thing Jagdalpur has to a hangout for the under-30 crowd.
eateries.insider_tip: Order one tribal dish (Farra or Tikhur) and one regular menu item; the Bastariya kitchen line is small and gets backed up if every table orders the regional menu. WiFi works, AC reliable.
eateries.signature_address: Near Dalpat Sagar Lake, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494001

eateries.name: Aamcho Bastar Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: The only sit-down restaurant on the Bastar tourism circuit cooking actual Bastariya tribal food - run by two local women chefs from the surrounding villages - and the reason a Chitrakote day-trip stops being a roadside-photo exercise.
eateries.insider_tip: Custom meals through Instagram (@amcho_bastar_cafe) - mahua, chapra (red ant chutney), and seasonal forest greens need a day's notice. Better lunch than dinner; light fades early at the falls.
eateries.signature_address: Entrance road, Chitrakote Falls, near Lohandiguda, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494223

eateries.name: Hari Om Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Steady-trade pure-veg multi-cuisine in a narrow alley off the main bazaar - the place Jagdalpur's Marwari and Punjabi families rotate through and Naman Bastar's own breakfast guests sometimes prefer.
eateries.insider_tip: Small room, peak hours 13:00-14:30 and 20:00-21:30 mean a queue. Order the flavoured sodas; they're a Jagdalpur quirk and most travellers miss them.
eateries.signature_address: Main Bazaar narrow lane, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494001

eateries.name: Mahavir Paratha Center
eateries.why_it_matters: The 9am paratha stop near Maa Danteshwari temple - where Jagdalpur's office-going crowd grabs breakfast before the Bastar district secretariat opens.
eateries.insider_tip: Get there before 9:30am or you queue. Sattu paratha is the local order, not aloo. Cash and UPI both work; outdoor benches only.
eateries.signature_address: Near Maa Danteshwari Temple, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494001

eateries.name: Shahid Park Chowpatty
eateries.why_it_matters: The city's evening street-food cluster at Shahid Park - the chowpatty Jagdalpur families walk to after dinner for kulfi and pani puri.
eateries.insider_tip: Open evening only, 17:00 to 22:00. Carry small change; vendors run on cash. The pav bhaji stalls peak around 19:30; arrive earlier to avoid the queue.
eateries.signature_address: Shahid Park, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494001

stays.name: Naman Bastar
stays.why_special: Best property in Bastar. Near Chitrakote Falls (India's Niagara). Tribal immersion.

picks.name: Dandami Luxury Resort Chitrakote
picks.why_nakshiq: At Chitrakote Falls — India's Niagara. Eco-resort format with waterfall-view cottages, CG Tourism-managed. 38 km from Jagdalpur. The distinctive Bastar stay for travelers wanting waterfall immersion over city-centre proximity.
picks.signature_experience: Dawn at Chitrakote Falls from the resort's viewpoint — 300m-wide horseshoe falls at peak flow (post-monsoon Oct-Dec); evening boat to the base.

picks.name: Hotel Abaad
picks.why_nakshiq: Central location with clean rooms, reliable WiFi, and staff who know the local Bastar tribal markets and sites—consistent 4.2-star ratings.

picks.name: Jagdalpur Tourist Rest House
picks.why_nakshiq: Run by Chhattisgarh Tourism Board, it sits on the banks of the Indravati River with walking distance to the main bazaar, colonial-era charm, and the best-priced river views.

picks.name: Bastar Village Homestay (Antagarh)
picks.why_nakshiq: Stay with a Gond tribal family 40 km south of Jagdalpur, participate in daily farming, learn traditional cooking, and sleep in a mud-and-thatch house—the lived experience of Bastar culture.

eateries.name: Hiuen Tsiang Tourist Resort Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Functionally the only sit-down restaurant in Sirpur village - inside the CG Tourism resort that sits 800m from the Lakshmana Temple, and the default lunch stop for visitors who came on the Raipur day-loop.
eateries.insider_tip: Order Chhattisgarhi thali if available rather than the standard Indian-Chinese. Mains ₹90-170. The 300-seater hall doubles as a wedding venue; on those days food times can stretch.
eateries.signature_address: Hiuen Tsiang Tourist Resort, Sirpur, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh 493554

eateries.name: Sirpur Village Dhabas
eateries.why_it_matters: Two or three village dhabas at the Sirpur bus stop run by local Telia and Patel families - the only food economy beyond the CG Tourism resort, and the only place a labourer working on the ASI digs would take a tea break.
eateries.insider_tip: Order pakhala (cooked rice steeped overnight in water with curd and lemon) if you visit between March-July - it is the genuine summer staple of central Chhattisgarh and rarely makes it onto restaurant menus. Cash only.
eateries.signature_address: Sirpur bus stop, Sirpur Village, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh 493554

eateries.name: Mahanadi Riverside Tea Stalls, Gandheshwar Ghat
eateries.why_it_matters: A row of one or two morning chai stalls at the Gandheshwar temple's Mahanadi ghat - what the temple priests' wives walk down to after the 6am aarti, and the calmest food moment in the village.
eateries.insider_tip: Mornings only, 6am-10am. After the river puja, the stalls shut by mid-morning. Bring your own snack as backup; opening days are weather-dependent.
eateries.signature_address: Gandheshwar Temple Ghat, Mahanadi riverside, Sirpur, Mahasamund District 493554

eateries.name: Mahasamund-Sirpur Highway Roadside Stalls
eateries.why_it_matters: The roadside stall cluster at the Sirpur turn-off from NH-53 - a Raipur-Sambalpur highway snack stop that is almost always more reliable than waiting for Sirpur village to find evening food.
eateries.insider_tip: Chana samosa - a Chhattisgarh specific - is the order. Pre-fried; ask for the freshest batch. Avoid post-21:00; stalls wind down with the highway truck flow.
eateries.signature_address: NH-53 Sirpur diversion, between Mahasamund and Sirpur village, Mahasamund District, Chhattisgarh

eateries.name: Sirpur Mahotsav Food Stalls
eateries.why_it_matters: During the three-day Sirpur Mahotsav (annually in late February), Chhattisgarh Tourism puts up a food court that stocks the regional dishes - chausela roti, aamat, mahua sweets - that almost never make it onto local restaurant menus the rest of the year.
eateries.insider_tip: Festival window only - typically last week of February. 2024 dates were 24-26 February. Outside this window the festival ground is empty; check Chhattisgarh Tourism for current year confirmation before timing a trip around it.
eateries.signature_address: Sirpur Mahotsav grounds, near Lakshmana Temple, Sirpur, Mahasamund District 493554

picks.name: Hareli Eco Resort, Mohda
picks.why_nakshiq: Forest-edge eco-resort at Mohda, 35 km from Sirpur - close enough to combine the archaeology day with a Barnawapara safari morning, and the pairing most Raipur-based travellers actually do. Rooms overlook a tank inside Barnawapara's buffer; the Sirpur drive is on a clean two-lane road.

picks.name: Hiuen Tsiang Tourist Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: The 19-room CG Tourism resort 800m from the Lakshmana Temple, named for the 7th-century Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who recorded Sirpur in his Da Tang Xiyu Ji. The only sit-down lodging at the site itself - and the only way to be on the monuments at sunrise without driving in from Raipur.

picks.name: Hiuen Tsiang Tourist Resort - Dorm
picks.why_nakshiq: The same CG Tourism resort runs two 15-bedded dorms alongside its private rooms - the cheapest legitimate stay in Sirpur and the only option at the village price band that won't fall apart on monsoon nights. Used by archaeology students and researchers on site visits.
